newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on U.S. long bond, peso.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on U.S. long bond, peso.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed up 75 basis points at 22.00 percent on Monday in response to a sharp gain in U.S. long bond yields and a soft peso, traders said.

"(U.S.) long bond yields are very high and that exerted some pressure on the market," a trader said. Yields on U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds stood at 7.10 percent on Wednesday, sharply up from 7.00 percent last Wednesday before markets closed for the Easter weekend in Mexico.
"Skittish U.S. markets are hitting us...the peso was also under pressure," another trader said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 1.4 centavos weaker at 7.9100/7.9140 per dollar.
Another trader put the increase in secondary interest rates down to speculation triggered by higher U.S. long bond yields.
"The (U.S. long) bond and speculation put pressure on the market, nothing else," he said.
Dealers agreed high U.S. long bond yields could maintain pressure on the local market for the remainder of the week.
Overnight rates on bank paper, meanwhile, closed up 85 basis points at 23.40 percent.
Banco de Mexico drained 942 million pesos from the secondary market through two auctions, which it assigned at 23.49 and 23.59 percent.
Liquidity of 2.271 billion pesos was slated to return to the system on Tuesday from prior central bank participation.
